Backward Compatibility: Working with Legacy Code

T. Florian Jaeger

Source: vignettes/backward-compatibility-working-with-legacy-code.Rmd
backward-compatibility-working-with-legacy-code.Rmd

Introduction and Architectural Shift

Earlier versions (pre-v1.0 / pre-v0.1.0) of MVBeliefUpdatr represented multidimensional category distributions, category templates, and cognitive decision models as nested tibble data frames with list-columns of vectors and parameter matrices (mu, Sigma, m, S, etc.). While convenient for simple tabular wrangling, weakly typed tabular models suffered from several limitations:

  • Lack of parameter dimension and positive-definiteness validation at object creation.
  • Loosely coupled model metadata, cue labels, decision rules, and noise parameters.
  • Dispersed and ad-hoc method dispatch across functions and packages.

Version 1.0 rebuilds MVBeliefUpdatr around R’s modern S7 object system, providing formal class definitions, robust property validators, unified generics, and a decoupled model family registry (MVBU_Family).

To provide a smooth, non-breaking transition path for existing analysis pipelines and user scripts, MVBeliefUpdatr provides an extensive compatibility bridge implemented in R/S7-to-legacy-tibble-compatibility.R and deprecation mappings.

library(MVBeliefUpdatr)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)

1. Coercing S7 Objects with as_tibble()

Calling as_tibble() on any modern S7 category representation, category template, or cognitive model produces a tibble matching the pre-S7 column schema, variable names, types, and column ordering:

# Create an S7 cognitive model
observer_model <- example_mvg_ideal_observer()

# Coerce an S7 cognitive model to a legacy tibble
model_tibble <- as_tibble(observer_model)
model_tibble
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   category mu           Sigma         prior lapse_rate lapse_bias Sigma_noise
#>   <fct>    <named list> <named list>  <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> <list>     
#> 1 /b/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]> 0.167          0      0.167 <NULL>     
#> 2 /d/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]> 0.167          0      0.167 <NULL>     
#> 3 /g/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]> 0.167          0      0.167 <NULL>     
#> 4 /k/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]> 0.167          0      0.167 <NULL>     
#> 5 /p/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]> 0.167          0      0.167 <NULL>     
#> 6 /t/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]> 0.167          0      0.167 <NULL>

# Inspect column names and list-column contents
names(model_tibble)
#> [1] "category"    "mu"          "Sigma"       "prior"       "lapse_rate" 
#> [6] "lapse_bias"  "Sigma_noise"
model_tibble$mu
#> $`/b/`

When called, as_tibble() issues an informative deprecation warning noting that S7 objects are the canonical format and that behavioral metadata (such as decision noise parameters, lapses, and internal validators) are not fully represented in tabular form.

2. Deprecated dplyr Verb Forwarding

For legacy workflows that previously piped models directly into dplyr verbs (e.g., model %>% mutate(...) or model %>% filter(...)), S3 method forwarding intercepts these calls, converts the object to a tibble, applies the requested verb, and alerts the user:

# Legacy workflow: calling filter() or select() on an S7 model
filtered_df <- suppressWarnings(filter(observer_model, category == "/i/"))
filtered_df
#> # A tibble: 0 × 7
#> # ℹ 7 variables: category <fct>, mu <named list>, Sigma <named list>,
#> #   prior <dbl>, lapse_rate <dbl>, lapse_bias <dbl>, Sigma_noise <list>

selected_df <- suppressWarnings(select(observer_model, category, mu, Sigma))
selected_df
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   category mu           Sigma        
#>   <fct>    <named list> <named list> 
#> 1 /b/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]>
#> 2 /d/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]>
#> 3 /g/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]>
#> 4 /k/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]>
#> 5 /p/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]>
#> 6 /t/      <dbl [1]>    <dbl [1 × 1]>

3. Parameter & Moment Accessors

In pre-v0.1.0 code, parameters were typically extracted by indexing list-columns:

# Legacy workflow (pre-v0.1.0):
mu_cat1 <- model_df$mu[[1]]
Sigma_cat1 <- model_df$Sigma[[1]]

In the modern S7 architecture, parameters and distributional moments are standardized via uniform S7 generics, described next.

Extracting Model Parameters (get_parameters)

The get_parameters() generic retrieves the structured named list of parameters guaranteed by the metadata$parameters property across all four architectural tiers:

# Extract parameters across a cognitive model
params_model <- get_parameters(observer_model)
params_model
#> $`/b/`
#> $`/b/`$mu
#> [1] 8.39663
#> 
#> $`/b/`$Sigma
#>          VOT
#> VOT 23.85665
#> 
#> 
#> $`/d/`
#> $`/d/`$mu
#> [1] 13.81306
#> 
#> $`/d/`$Sigma
#>          VOT
#> VOT 77.63595
#> 
#> 
#> $`/g/`
#> $`/g/`$mu
#> [1] 16.71445
#> 
#> $`/g/`$Sigma
#>          VOT
#> VOT 108.7265
#> 
#> 
#> $`/k/`
#> $`/k/`$mu
#> [1] 54.04223
#> 
#> $`/k/`$Sigma
#>          VOT
#> VOT 418.7947
#> 
#> 
#> $`/p/`
#> $`/p/`$mu
#> [1] 50.23845
#> 
#> $`/p/`$Sigma
#>          VOT
#> VOT 445.1705
#>

#>

# Extract parameters from an individual category representation
rep_first <- observer_model@category_template@representations[[1]]
get_parameters(rep_first)
#> $mu
#> [1] 8.39663
#> 
#> $Sigma
#>          VOT
#> VOT 23.85665

Accessing Expected and Marginal Moments

For Bayesian belief distributions (such as NIW, NIX, and MNIX ideal adaptors), distributional moments are accessed directly through dedicated generics rather than manually computed from hyperparameters (κ,ν,m,S\kappa, \nu, m, S):

# Instantiate an NIW ideal adaptor model
adaptor_model <- example_niw_ideal_adaptor()

# Expected moments conditional on hyperparameter beliefs:
get_expected_mu(adaptor_model)
#> $`/b/`
#> [1] 8.39663
#> 
#> $`/d/`
#> [1] 13.81306
#> 
#> $`/g/`
#> [1] 16.71445
#> 
#> $`/k/`
#> [1] 54.04223
#> 
#> $`/p/`
#> [1] 50.23845
#> 
#> $`/t/`
#> [1] 60.48317
get_expected_sigma(adaptor_model)
#> $`/b/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 23.85665
#> 
#> $`/d/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 77.63595
#> 
#> $`/g/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 108.7265
#> 
#> $`/k/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 418.7947
#> 
#> $`/p/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 445.1705
#> 
#> $`/t/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 476.4007

# Marginal moments incorporating estimation uncertainty:
get_marginal_mu(adaptor_model)
#> $`/b/`
#> [1] 8.39663
#> 
#> $`/d/`
#> [1] 13.81306
#> 
#> $`/g/`
#> [1] 16.71445
#> 
#> $`/k/`
#> [1] 54.04223
#> 
#> $`/p/`
#> [1] 50.23845
#> 
#> $`/t/`
#> [1] 60.48317
get_marginal_sigma(adaptor_model)
#> $`/b/`
#>         [,1]
#> [1,] 47.7133
#> 
#> $`/d/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 155.2719
#> 
#> $`/g/`
#>         [,1]
#> [1,] 217.453
#> 
#> $`/k/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 837.5894
#> 
#> $`/p/`
#>         [,1]
#> [1,] 890.341
#> 
#> $`/t/`
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 952.8014

4. Transitioning Collections of Models to MVBU_ModelList

In legacy workflows, researchers often tracked model adaptation across trials, blocks, or experimental conditions by storing models inside tibbles:

# Legacy workflow:
history_tbl <- tibble(
  step = 1:2,
  model = list(model_step1, model_step2)
)

In modern MVBeliefUpdatr, collections of models are represented using the typed MVBU_ModelList class:

# Construct a typed collection of cognitive models
model_seq <- MVBU_ModelList(
  models = list(observer_model, adaptor_model),
  model_labels = c("Initial_Observer", "Adapted_Model")
)
model_seq
#> <MVBU_ModelList>

# Subsetting returns an MVBU_ModelList or individual model:
model_seq[1]
#> <MVBU_ModelList>
model_seq[[1]]
#> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MVG_IdealObserver>
#>   Categories (6): /b/, /d/, /g/, /k/, /p/, /t/
#>   Cues (1): VOT
#>   Decision rule: sampling
#>   Category prior: /b/: 0.167, /d/: 0.167, /g/: 0.167, /k/: 0.167, /p/: 0.167, /t/: 0.167
#>   Lapse rate: 0 (treatment: no_lapses)
#>   Perceptual noise: none (treatment: no_noise)
#>   Category representations (6):
#>     /b/: MVG(mu = 8.397, Sigma = 23.86)
#>     /d/: MVG(mu = 13.81, Sigma = 77.64)
#>     /g/: MVG(mu = 16.71, Sigma = 108.7)
#>     /k/: MVG(mu = 54.04, Sigma = 418.8)
#>     /p/: MVG(mu = 50.24, Sigma = 445.2)
#>     /t/: MVG(mu = 60.48, Sigma = 476.4)
model_seq[["Adapted_Model"]]
#> NULL

# Batch parameter extraction across all models:
get_parameters(model_seq)
#> list()

MVBU_ModelList objects integrate directly with plot_categories() and plot_categorization_functions() for visualizing incremental belief updating trajectories.

5. API Migration Mapping Table

The table below maps legacy (pre-v0.1.0) functions and naming conventions to their modern v0.1.0+ S7 API replacements. All legacy functions issue deprecation warnings in v0.1.0 and are scheduled for removal in v0.2.0.

Legacy API Concept / Function (pre-v0.1.0) Modern S7 API Replacement (v0.1.0+) Description / Purpose
make_MVG_from_data() new_mvg_category_representation_template_from_data() Estimate MVG category template from data
make_MVG_ideal_observer_from_data() new_mvg_ideal_observer_from_data() Construct MVG cognitive model from data
make_NIW_belief_from_data() new_niw_category_representation_template_from_data() Estimate NIW belief template from data
make_NIW_ideal_adaptor_from_data() new_niw_ideal_adaptor_from_data() Construct NIW ideal adaptor model from data
make_NIX_belief_from_data() new_nix_category_representation_template_from_data() Estimate NIX belief template from data
make_NIX_ideal_adaptor_from_data() new_nix_ideal_adaptor_from_data() Construct NIX ideal adaptor model from data
make_MNIX_belief_from_data() new_mnix_category_representation_template_from_data() Estimate MNIX belief template from data
make_MNIX_ideal_adaptor_from_data() new_mnix_ideal_adaptor_from_data() Construct MNIX ideal adaptor model from data
make_exemplars_from_data() new_exemplar_category_representation_template_from_data() Estimate Exemplar category template from data
make_exemplar_model_from_data() new_exemplar_model_from_data() Construct Exemplar model from data
lift_MVG_to_MVG_ideal_observer() lift_representation_to_model() / new_mvg_ideal_observer() Wrap MVG category template in cognitive model
lift_NIW_belief_to_NIW_ideal_adaptor() lift_representation_to_model() / new_niw_ideal_adaptor() Wrap NIW template in ideal adaptor model
lift_NIX_belief_to_NIX_ideal_adaptor() lift_representation_to_model() / new_nix_ideal_adaptor() Wrap NIX template in ideal adaptor model
lift_MNIX_belief_to_MNIX_ideal_adaptor() lift_representation_to_model() / new_mnix_ideal_adaptor() Wrap MNIX template in ideal adaptor model
lift_exemplars_to_exemplar_model() lift_representation_to_model() / new_exemplar_model() Wrap Exemplar template in cognitive model
is.ideal_adaptor_stanfit() S7::S7_inherits(x, IdealAdaptorStanfit) Type check for S7 Stanfit objects
read_ideal_adaptor_stanfit() read_stanfit() Read saved Stanfit object from RDS
write_ideal_adaptor_stanfit() write_stanfit() Write Stanfit object to RDS
get_info_from_model() get_parameters(), summary(), or as_tibble() Extract model parameters / metadata
get_model_family() get_family_name() / get_family() Retrieve model family name or MVBU_Family
get_representation_type() get_family_name() Retrieve representation family name
sample_observation() sample_observations() Draw random samples from category representations
prepare_staninput() new_ideal_adaptor_stanfit_input() Prepare typed input for ideal adaptor Stan models
x_ss / c_ss x_css / c_css Centered sum of squares in sufficient statistics
Nested model tibbles MVBU_ModelList Typed collections of cognitive models
